thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: nvaddr-validation failure detected -> downstream CUDA illegal-memory-access errors on serving-prod-6 and serving-prod-7. Threshold exceeded for invalid-device-address metric. Auto-remediation triggered: scale-down attempted, failed on node 6.

leo_oncall: ack, I'm taking. quick status please — customer-facing routes affected? @ryan_support can you confirm impact? :rotating_light:

ryan_support: seeing elevated 5xx for /generate on eu-west region. ~18% error rate past 7m, retries causing latency spikes. Affected customers: two mid-market tenants on dedicated pools (IDs redacted).

sara_infra: cordoning nodes now: `kubectl cordon serving-prod-6 && kubectl cordon serving-prod-7` and starting drain on 7 (grace 60s). Noting that 6 refuses drain due to ongoing GPU attachments.

maria_ml: logs from model container on serving-prod-6: `cudaErrorIllegalAddress: invalid device pointer at inference_kernel.cu:243` followed by kernel OOPS from dmesg: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU page fault at address 0x7fffa12b0000 (reason: misaligned address)`. Repro rate: intermittent under long-context loads.

aj_runtime: forwarding to runtime team. immediate mitigation: route new requests to cpu-fallback pool and enable model-variant fallback in routing policy. Runbook step 3: set `routing.fallback.priority=cpu` for affected model route.

leo_oncall: can we push routing change now? we need to reduce customer errors quickly.

aj_runtime: applying change: `rbac patch /routes/model-xyz -p '{"fallback":"cpu"}'` — done. Confirming traffic shift ~2m.

ryan_support: error rate dropped to 2.1% within 3m after fallback. Latency up ~120ms on CPU variant but customers recovering. I'll notify impacted tenants with interim ETA.

sara_infra: still troubleshooting why node 6 won't drain — kernel logs show repeated pagewalk retries and SMMU entries flickering. Dumping coredump: `/var/crash/gpu-6-2026-03-15.tgz` and uploading to /shared/incidents/6942001234.

maria_ml: initial triage: suspect kernel-level GPU driver regression exposing a race when KV cache flush overlaps with large KV map; triggering misaligned device pointers in runtime. Need deeper DFIR with vendor NUMA/SMMU team.

leo_oncall: escalation plan: 1) keep CPU fallback for customer stability, 2) maintain cordon on 6/7, 3) escalate to vendor with logs + dmesg, 4) schedule rolling drain/reboot once vendor provides handshake or workaround. I'll open an incident ticket and add executive summary.

ops-bot: INCIDENT TICKET CREATED: INC-694200-2026 -> nvaddr-validation failure. Assigned: aj_runtime, sara_infra. Severity: SEV2 (customer impact but mitigation in place).

leo_oncall: Quick summary for execs: transient GPU pagewalk/misaligned-device-address causing cuda illegal-addresses on two serving nodes; automated fallback to CPU reduced errors; ongoing investigation with vendor for kernel/driver race. I'll post a customer-facing blurb in 30m. :white_check_mark:

maria_ml: note for postmortem — capture exact sequence: long-context request -> KV map grow -> concurrent cache flush -> driver pagewalk -> invalid device pointer. Add prompt set and token length for failing requests to repro.

ryan_support: FYI I've informed impacted customers and offered temporary credits; they acknowledged and requested final RCA.

leo_oncall: thanks all. keeping thread open for vendor updates and repro attempts.
